title: Sensory acuity and cross-language phonetic similarity jointly predict second language vowel production accuracy
task: repeated isolated Mandarin /u/ and /y/ production plus English/novel-vowel somatosensory production tasks
token_or_recording_size: 40 English-speaking adult late learners of Mandarin; repeated target-vowel productions; exact repository row count pending file audit
annotation_target: vowel onset/offset; F1/F2 midpoint; formant-track quality; production accuracy/variability; English /ae/, /ɑ/ and novel-vowel productions for somatosensory task
manual_scope: Praat intensity-based onset/offset proposed automatically, then experimenter visually inspected every vowel boundary and manually corrected when needed; formant-track/spectrogram alignment visually inspected with speaker/vowel-specific LPC selection; F1/F2 outliers visually inspected and manually corrected
decision_reason: Primary controlled L2 production dataset with public OSF deposit and explicit exhaustive visual inspection/manual correction of relevant vowel boundaries and acoustic formant measurements.
evidence_summary: Frontiers methods report 40 English-speaking adult late learners producing Mandarin /u/ and /y/. Each automatically proposed vowel onset/offset was visually inspected and manually corrected if needed; formant tracking was checked against the spectrogram and outlier F1/F2 values were visually inspected and manually corrected. Data availability gives OSF 9qt5j.
